item.title: Kestrel: QoS Anomaly Detection in 5G User Planes
item.description:
Kestrel is an ongoing research effort on detecting QoS anomalies in the 5G user plane.
Issues such as congestion, microbursts, and policy abuse can degrade user experience within seconds, yet existing telemetry methods are either too coarse or too costly. Kestrel investigates how to gain the needed visibility while keeping monitoring overhead practical.

item.title: SliceScope: SLA-Aware Monitoring in 5G Slices
item.description:
SliceScope is an ongoing research effort on SLA-aware monitoring for 5G network slices.
Guaranteeing SLAs demands visibility that can adapt to rapidly changing conditions, yet current approaches are either too coarse or too costly.
SliceScope investigates how to provide accurate, adaptive monitoring that enables early detection of violations without incurring excessive overhead.

item.title: Preprint: NWDAF-Enabled Analytics in 5G Networks
item.description:
Managing 5G networks at scale demands automation that can adapt in real time, yet existing tools struggle to combine standardized data collection, machine learning integration, and closed-loop control.

Our ongoing work addresses this gap by exploring how the 3GPP Network Data Analytics Function (NWDAF) can be realized in practice to support low-latency, scalable, and intelligent network management. The approach shows promise for use cases such as anomaly detection, security, and policy enforcement.

item.title: AmbuSens IoT based Ubiquitous Healthcare Monitoring
item.description:
The AmbuSens system was developed at the Smart Wireless Applications and Networking (SWAN) Lab at the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, India.

AmbuSens focuses on achieving seamless real-time monitoring and management of healthcare data in an ambulatory context, leveraging IoT technologies such as wireless on-body sensors, cellular (3G/4G), and cloud computing. The system leverages wireless body area network (WBAN) to wirelessly collect various physiological health parameters (e.g., ECG and heart rate). The collected data is processed by a middleware solution that uses an unique hashing-based privacy-preservation mechanism to preserve patient’s confidentiality before subsequent transmission and storage in the cloud.
